content: Acidophilus refers to a group of probiotic microorganisms that are commonly incorporated into milk products or sold in capsule form. These probiotics include one or more of the following bacterial strains, which are known to support digestive health: Lactobacillus acidophilus (A): This is the true acidophilus strain and is the most accurately referred to as acidophilus. Lactobacillus casei (C): A beneficial bacterium that aids in digestion and supports gut health. Lactobacillus bulgaricus (L): A strain often used in the fermentation of yogurt and other dairy products. Bifidobacterium bifidum (B): A probiotic that contributes to maintaining a healthy balance of gut flora. Streptococcus thermophilus: A bacterium frequently used in the production of yogurt and cheese, which also has probiotic properties. Although only Lactobacillus acidophilus is the true acidophilus strain, many manufacturers, particularly in the United States, use the term acidophilus more broadly to describe mixtures of bacteria that include Lactobacillus acidophilus as one of the components. Acidophilus can naturally occur in certain high-quality yogurts and other traditional fermented foods. For more detailed information, it is recommended to review the specific characteristics of each bacterial strain and consult resources on probiotics.
